groups: FX: any number (each track its own)
FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)

items.label: keep at least this much undo history
items.desc: Keeps headroom for the undo history instead of filling RAM and pool to the last byte: the history's ring is what they leave free ((98,304 - RAM) + (344,064 - 8,192 - pool), docs/MEMORY-MAP.md). The estimate shows the ring and warns below this figure; a build whose real ring is smaller is refused. Nothing in the firmware changes (it needs the undo / redo history item).

items.label: keep at least this much app flash free
items.desc: Keeps room in the app slot for later (a feature, an update) instead of filling it to the last byte: the budget subtracts it from the slot and a build that leaves less free is refused. Nothing in the firmware changes.

items.label: ANALOG 2 (analog-style synth, swarm, 2 filters)
items.desc: The main subtractive synth: two oscillators with hard sync, a swarm of up to 6 detuned copies (supersaw), two filters. About 6 KB of flash and 4.7 KB of fast RAM code; it is also the stand-in that most other engines fall back to, so keep it unless you need the space.

items.label: DIGITAL (4-operator FM)
items.desc: Four-operator FM synth: 8 classic algorithms, feedback on operator 4 and one modulation INDEX with its own envelope. About 2 KB of flash; the stand-in for FM6 when FM6 is left out.

items.label: PHASE (phase distortion)
items.desc: Phase-distortion synth: bends the phase of a cosine wave to get saw, square, pulse and resonant shapes with a second line to mix or ring-modulate. About 1.4 KB of flash; the stand-in for CZ.

items.label: LOFI (chip sounds, wavetable)
items.desc: Chip voice: pulse, triangle, saw, noise and a 4-bit wavetable, with a few-bit amplitude, a held (low) sample rate and a pitch sweep. About 2 KB of flash.

items.label: SAMPLE (sample sets, USR slots)
items.desc: Plays the built-in sample sets and your own samples (USR1..USR3 slots) across the keyboard, with loops. About 1.4 KB of flash plus the sets you keep (see Sample sets); it is also the stand-in for GRAIN and SLICE.

items.label: VOICE (formant, sung vowels)
items.desc: Formant synth that sings vowels from the keyboard (4 voices; BUZZ and BREATH shape the voice). About 2.7 KB of flash; a special sound, leave it out if you need the space.

items.label: TRIO (3 oscillators)
items.desc: Three oscillators with ring modulation and hard sync into a multimode filter, in the style of early 8-bit home-computer sound chips. About 3.4 KB of flash.

items.label: WHEEL (drawbar organ)
items.desc: Tonewheel-style organ: nine sine drawbars per note, 16 registrations to choose from. About 2.3 KB of flash and 2.5 KB of RAM.

items.label: GRAIN (granular on the sample sets)
items.desc: Granular synth: plays clouds of tiny grains cut from the sample sets or your USR slots. About 4.9 KB of flash and 21 KB of pool; with no sample set built it plays your USR samples only.

items.label: FM6 (DX7, bit-exact with Dexed)
items.desc: Six-operator FM that plays Yamaha DX7 voices the way the Dexed plug-in does, with its own operator editor and DX7 SysEx. The biggest engine: about 32 KB of flash, 10 KB of RAM and 12 KB of pool; its options below trim it down.
items.provenance_line: Melodee (keremimo/melodee) @ e459da5 by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: FM6 mode MARK I (DX7's own tables)
items.desc: The FM6 ENGINE mode that uses the DX7's own log-sine and exponent tables and its feedback behaviour, for the most DX7-like sound. Costs about 3.2 KB of flash and 4.1 KB of RAM; off: voices asking for it play another mode you kept.

items.label: FM6 MARK I tables in flash
items.desc: with MARK I: its log-sine and exponent tables as generated const data in flash instead of RAM tables built at boot (4 KB of RAM less, 1.9 KB of flash more). CPU cost on the FM-1 unknown: the emulator models neither the XIP cache nor flash wait states
items.notice: measured in the emulator only, which has no XIP cache and no flash wait states; on the FM-1 every MARK I operator sample reads flash twice: the CPU cost there is not measured.

items.label: FM6 mode MODERN (clean 24-bit)
items.desc: The FM6 ENGINE mode with Dexed's modern 24-bit maths (MSFA). Costs only about 0.6 KB of flash (the sine table stays: the LFO uses it); keep at least one of the three modes.

items.label: FM6 mode OPL (grittier, chip resolution)
items.desc: The FM6 ENGINE mode with the resolution of Yamaha OPL chips, for a different tone from the DX7 modes. Costs about 1.9 KB of flash and 1.5 KB of RAM (tables).

items.label: FM6 operator editor on the black keys
items.desc: Edit a DX7 voice on the device: hold ENV and press a black key to pick an operator, the pitch envelope or the global page, then turn the knobs. About 7.8 KB of flash; off: voices can only be changed by DX7 SysEx or the web editor.

items.label: FM6 DX7 SysEx in / SEND (web editor FM6 tab)
items.desc: Accepts DX7 voice, bank and parameter changes over USB MIDI, so Dexed or any DX7 librarian can edit a part live, and can SEND the voice back; the web editor's FM6 tab needs it. About 1.2 KB of flash; its 4.1 KB RAM buffer is shared with STORE.

items.label: FM6 16 factory voices R01..R16
items.desc: The 16 built-in DX7 voices R01..R16 (about 2 KB of flash). Off: the R slots play INIT VOICE, a plain starting voice; your own bank (U voices) is not affected.

items.label: FM6 operator editor in VIEW ALL (pages as rows)
items.desc: with VIEW ALL: an operator's pages (or PIT, GLO) as rows of 4 x 4 PAGEs; off: one page at a time (saves about 1.2 KB of flash)

items.label: FM6 algorithm full screen (hold ENV)
items.desc: Holding ENV a while on an FM6 track shows the algorithm full screen, with operators numbered and carriers, modulators and the feedback loop told apart. Only 48 B of flash; off: holding ENV does nothing extra.

items.label: FM6 user bank STORE (U01..U32 in a USR slot)
items.desc: STORE your edited voices into a user bank of 32 (U01..U32), kept in a USR sample slot. About 0.6 KB of flash and 0.5 KB of RAM; off: no user bank (STORE says NO USER BANK).

items.label: FM6 / CZ native tone collections in PRESETS
items.desc: An FM6 or CZ track's PRESETS list ends with its engine's own tones: FM6 U01..U32 (the FM6 user bank) and, with CZ, a collection of 26 CZ-1 tones (the web editor imports and exports Casio .syx). Loading one sets only the engine's values: the track keeps its FX, mix and pattern. With CZ the collection takes 8 KiB at USR3's end (USR3 holds that much less). About 0.6 KB of flash, 2 KB with CZ (measured); no RAM.
items.provenance_line: Melodee (keremimo/melodee) @ v0.12 18bfd53 by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: SLICE (break slicer + its BREAK sample)
items.desc: Break slicer: cuts a loop (the built-in BREAK, 22 KB of samples, or a USR slot) into 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 slices or one per hit and plays them from the keys or the sequencer. About 27 KB of flash and 6 KB of RAM; off by default.
items.provenance_line: Felucca (hugelton/Felucca) by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: drum synth (all 32 synthesised kits)
items.desc: The 32 synthesised drum kits (808, 909 and others), generated by the firmware, so they take no sample memory. About 13.7 KB of flash; the drum track needs this or at least one sampled kit.

items.label: sampled drums (the PERC set, 99 KB)
items.desc: The recorded drum samples (the PERC set, about 99 KB of flash) behind the five sampled kits below. Switching this off drops all of them; the drum track then needs the drum synth.

items.label: sampled kit ACOUSTIC
items.desc: The sampled kit as recorded (the basic kit of the PERC set). It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit DEEP
items.desc: The sampled kit tuned down and softened by a low-pass filter: a darker, heavier kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit TIGHT
items.desc: The sampled kit with every hit cut short by a fast decay: a dry, punchy kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit BRIGHT
items.desc: The sampled kit tuned two semitones up: a lighter kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit DUST
items.desc: The sampled kit tuned slightly down, filtered and reduced to a coarse bit depth: a gritty lo-fi kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: drum sound editor (EDIT on the drum track)
items.desc: Per-lane sound tweaks over the kit (TUNE, DECAY, SNAP, CLICK, BEND, CUT, DRIVE, LEVEL on synthesised kits; TUNE, DECAY, CUT, LEVEL on sampled ones). About 1.2 KB of flash; off: kits play as they are and saved tweaks are kept but not applied.

items.label: user samples on drum lanes
items.desc: A drum lane can play one of your own samples (a hit of a USR slot, with start and length) instead of the kit's sound. About 1.2 KB of flash; off: such lanes play the kit sound.

items.label: user drum kits (bank of 16 in data flash)
items.desc: Lane sources from other kits and the X0X machines, and a bank of 16 user kits (each lane's source and sound tweaks) saved in flash. About 2.8 KB of flash; off: lanes play the kit as it is.

items.label: X0X 909 kit (circuit-modelled TR-909)
items.desc: X0X's TR-909 drum kit (kit UID 37; the drum models are circuit-modelled, hi-hats, ride and crash are samples), on the 16 lanes; SHAKER, CONGA, COWBELL play the synthesised 909's. Big: about 151 KB of flash (see its cymbal option) and uses floating point; emulator-tested only. A build without it plays the synthesised 909 for it and keeps the kit
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), itself from 9W9 / 8W8 by athousanddetails and ER-99 by Matthew Cieplak (GPL-3.0); the 808's rim shot after sc808 (Yoshinosuke Horiuchi / Sam Aaron, MIT). Experimental in Optimist: float DSP, emulator-tested only.
items.provenance_line: X0X (charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) @ 80b7d40 by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: X0X 909: ride and crash sample quality
items.desc: 8-bit block floating point as before; 6-bit: 22 KB less, 30 dB against the 16-bit source instead of 42 (screens x0xdrums-perf-2026-10-06); off: RIDE and CRASH play the synthesised 909's (the hi-hat samples stay)

items.label: X0X 808 kit (circuit-modelled TR-808)
items.desc: X0X's TR-808 drum kit (kit UID 38; 16 circuit-modelled sounds) on the 16 lanes; MIDI also plays MT, LC, HC and the claves (note 75). About 30 KB of flash and uses floating point; emulator-tested only. A build without it plays the synthesised 808 for it and keeps the kit
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), itself from 9W9 / 8W8 by athousanddetails and ER-99 by Matthew Cieplak (GPL-3.0); the 808's rim shot after sc808 (Yoshinosuke Horiuchi / Sam Aaron, MIT). Experimental in Optimist: float DSP, emulator-tested only.
items.provenance_line: X0X (charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) @ 80b7d40 by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: drum ACCENT lane (909 style)
items.desc: A 17th step lane on the drum track, the ACCENT lane: no sound of its own, its steps raise every hit of the step by the drum track's ACCENT amount (0 to 127 velocity, default 27: a normal hit plays at full velocity), into each kit's own velocity response (the X0X 909 / 808: their accent input); MIDI out sends the raised velocity. It works as a lane: steps, levels, ratchets, chance and conditions, copy, erase, the STEP tools, patterns, sections, snapshots. Off: the lane is kept and edited but not heard. Needs the automation store (motion, locks, chance or conditions).

items.label: PIANO (Steinway, 44 KB)
items.desc: A grand piano, plus the dusty and lo-fi piano variants. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: BASS (39 KB)
items.desc: An upright bass, plus a deep bass variant. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: VIBES (33 KB)
items.desc: A vibraphone. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: HORNS (26 KB)
items.desc: Horn stabs. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: STRINGS (20 KB)
items.desc: String stabs. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: FLUTE (31 KB)
items.desc: A lo-fi flute. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: SCRATCH (23 KB)
items.desc: Turntable scratch hits. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: DIST (per-track drive)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A distortion on each synth track: low cut, drive from 1x to 8x into an asymmetric soft clip, and a tone filter that closes as the drive rises. About 0.4 KB of flash; off: the DIST controls disappear.

items.label: chorus
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The chorus effect, fed by each track's CHO send. About 0.4 KB of flash and 4 KB of pool; off: the CHO sends and the chorus settings disappear.

items.label: delay
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The tempo-synced delay (echo), fed by each track's DLY send. Costs 128 KB of the pool at the full length: shorten it with the length option, or leave it out.

items.label: delay length (how long an echo can be)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The longest delay time, which sets the pool memory the delay takes. A time longer than the line is halved until it fits, so it stays on the beat; shorter lines suit fast tempos only.

items.label: reverb
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The reverb, fed by each track's REV send and the drums' reverb, with its algorithms below (tick at least one). Each one ticked is on the device's FX > REVERB > TYPE and in the web editor's Reverb popup, switched while it plays; with one ticked there is no TYPE. They share one line buffer, sized to the largest. The biggest user of RAM among the FX (about 17 KB with ROOM); off: the REV sends and reverb settings disappear.

items.label: reverb: ROOM
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Four delay lines at 44.1 kHz, the reverb as it always was: sparse for its first ~300 ms (separate echoes, a grainy start), then the tail. Its 17 KB of lines set the shared buffer's size when it is ticked. Off, with another algorithm ticked: about 1.8 KB of flash, 2.4 KB of RAM and 2 KB of pool saved.

items.label: reverb: PLATE (Dattorro)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Dattorro's figure-of-eight plate at 22.05 kHz: dense from ~50 ms, a smooth decay, nothing above ~11 kHz, about 10 % fewer instructions than ROOM. A 16 KB ring (8 KB at half rate) in the shared buffer. Beside ROOM: about 2.9 KB of flash and 3.4 KB of RAM; with two or more algorithms each one's code runs from main RAM. Experimental: measured on the host and in the emulator only, not yet heard on an FM-1.
items.notice: PLATE: measured on the host and in the emulator only; not yet heard on an FM-1.

items.label: reverb: FDN8 (long, lush)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Long and lush: eight slowly modulated lines at 22.05 kHz, dense from ~50 ms, the widest and least ringing tail, nothing above ~11 kHz. Up to SIZE 90 the ROOM's decay; above it the decay doubles every 10 steps to ~14 s at 126 and a near-freeze at 127, the treble kept as DAMP says; about 20 % more instructions than ROOM. A 16 KB ring (8 KB at half rate) in the shared buffer. Beside ROOM: about 4.0 KB of flash and 4.3 KB of RAM (with PLATE too, 1.1 KB of flash and 1.8 KB of RAM are shared). Experimental: measured on the host and in the emulator only, not yet heard on an FM-1.
items.notice: FDN8: measured on the host and in the emulator only; not yet heard on an FM-1.

items.label: reverb: VTINY (Airwindows VerbTiny)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Airwindows' VerbTiny (Chris Johnson, MIT): sixteen lines in four 4 x 4 Householder stages, left and right in one loop, at 22.05 kHz. A plain early-digital texture: peakier and grainier than FDN8 (it is not modulated), dense from ~80 ms, ringing no more than the ROOM; nothing above ~11 kHz. SIZE as the ROOM's decay up to 90, then FDN8's long top (~11 s at 126, a near-freeze at 127); DAMP the ROOM's treble loss. Its lines fill the shared 16 KB ring (8 KB at half rate: a smaller room). About 40 % more instructions than FDN8. Beside ROOM: about 4.5 KB of flash and 6.5 KB of main RAM (the tanks' code runs from RAM), no pool past the shared ring (user-default has no flash left for it). Experimental: measured on the host only, not yet heard on an FM-1.
items.notice: VTINY: measured on the host only; not yet heard on an FM-1.

items.label: reverb buffers in the pool (saves ~17 KB RAM)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Keeps the reverb's shared line buffer (17 KB with ROOM, 8.7 KB at half rate; PLATE and FDN8 without ROOM 16 KB, 8 KB at half rate; SPRING alone 8 KB) in the pool instead of main RAM: main RAM is the scarcer, and the sound and the code stay the same. Needs that much pool free (the undo history shrinks by it in the pool and grows by it in RAM).

items.label: half-rate reverb (half the RAM, no top octave)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Runs the ROOM reverb at half the sample rate (22.05 kHz) behind a half-band filter: its memory takes half the RAM (-8.7 KB) and it costs less CPU, with the same decay and room size. PLATE and FDN8 already run at 22.05 kHz; here they get half the ring (8 KB), a smaller tank with more audible modes. The reverb loses its top octave (above ~11 kHz); the dry sound and the other buses are untouched.

items.label: SLICER (stutter / gate insert)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A tempo-synced 16-step gate or stutter on each track (not the sample slicer engine): chops the sound to a pattern. About 1.2 KB of flash and 32 KB of pool at the full capture length.

items.label: SLICER capture length (stutter memory)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: How much sound each track's stutter records to repeat: the shorter capture saves 16 KB of pool and limits how long a repeated chunk can be (the gate mode is unaffected).

items.label: PUNCH (16 punch-in FX)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Hold FX and press a white key to put the whole mix through one of 16 effects while it is held (loops, reverse, tape stop, half speed, wobble, echo, filters, crush, gate), beat-synced. About 2.3 KB of flash and 64 KB of pool at the full ring.

items.label: PUNCH memory length (how much mix it can loop)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: How much of the mix the loop, reverse, tape-stop and echo effects can capture; the shorter ring saves 32 KB of pool and cuts the longest loop in half.

items.label: DJ filter (MASTER FILT)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: One knob on the master (MASTER > FILT): turn left for a low-pass closing, right for a high-pass opening, centre is off. About 0.7 KB of flash.

items.label: DUST (vinyl / lo-fi master)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: One knob on the master (MASTER > DUST) that runs the mix through an old sampler and a record: drive, lower sample rate, fewer bits, a darker tone, hiss and crackle while playing. About 0.7 KB of flash.

items.label: DUCK (kick ducks the parts)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Pumping sidechain effect (MASTER > DUCK): every kick from the drum track dips the synth parts, which swell back over an eighth note. About 0.1 KB of flash; has no effect without a drum kick.

items.label: COMP + LIMIT (master compressor, brickwall limiter)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A compressor and a brickwall limiter on the master (GLO > COMP: THRS, RATIO, ATK, REL; GLO > LIMIT: GAIN, CEIL and a GR readout) to glue the mix and keep its peaks under a ceiling; a Comp button and a GR meter in the web mixer. A new project limits at CEIL -3.0 dB (a look-ahead limiter in place of the old one); saved projects keep their own CEIL (OFF: as before). About 2 KB of flash and 2.5 KB of RAM.

items.label: track FILTER (LP <- off -> HP on each track)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A DJ-style filter on each track: FX > FILTER (one knob, FILT: left low-pass, right high-pass, centre off) and FX held + KNOB 4 for the selected track. On the drum track it filters the summed drums and all their sends. Saved with the project, kept when the sound changes, recordable with motion. Costs nothing at the centre; engaged, one filter per track (five on the drum bus).
items.notice: From SLOOP 2.4's track filter by isod89 (isod89/sloop-fm1 v2.4, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: SLOOP 2.4 (isod89/sloop-fm1) @ v2.4 8d3823f by isod89 (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: FOLD insert (wavefolder)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A wavefolder type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: FOLD): the sound driven past full scale folds back, more folds and harmonics as FOLD rises; the drive follows the track's level as DIST's does, the bass stays dry. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT FOLD by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Felucca 1.5.6 (hugelton/Felucca) @ 9f6a885 by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: FUZZ insert
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A fuzz type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: FUZZ): a hard-clipped top and a soft, halved bottom (lopsided, buzzy), the drive with FUZZ. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT FUZZ by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Felucca 1.5.6 (hugelton/Felucca) @ 9f6a885 by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: PHSR insert (phaser)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A phaser type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: PHSR): four all-pass stages swept slowly (~0.5 Hz); PHSR up to the middle mixes it in, past the middle adds feedback. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT PHASR by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Felucca 1.5.6 (hugelton/Felucca) @ 9f6a885 by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: FRMT insert (vowel filter)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A vowel filter type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: FRMT): three formant peaks over the sound; FRMT moves the vowel from A (low) through E, I, O to U (high). 0 is off.
items.notice: From Melodee 1.3.1's FORMANT insert by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0); its vowel table, fixed point here. Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Melodee 1.3.1 (keremimo/melodee) @ next 757b65b by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: WIDE insert (stereo width)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A stereo width type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: WIDE): one side through slowly swept all-pass filters, the other dry, so a centred mono track spreads out; WIDE sets how much. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Melodee 1.3.1's WIDTH insert by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Melodee 1.3.1 (keremimo/melodee) @ next 757b65b by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: CHRS insert (chorus copies for the tracks)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A chorus type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: CHRS), beside the chorus send: two taps around 7 ms swept apart at ~0.8 Hz; CHRS up to the middle mixes it in, past the middle widens the sweep. On the drum track it turns the drums' mid into a stereo chorus. 0 is off. Each instance is a line in the pool; a track that picks it when every instance is in use stays dry until one is free (the INSERTS list shows how many are left). A saved project keeps the type, not the instance: on load the tracks get them in order T1 T2 T3 DR.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: ECHO insert (short delay copies for the tracks)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A slapback type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: ECHO), beside the delay send: one repeat 75 ms after the sound; ECHO up to the middle sets its level, past the middle adds repeats (feedback up to 60 %). Up to 93 ms of line an instance (the long, tempo-synced delay stays the send's). 0 is off. Each instance is a line in the pool; a track that picks it when every instance is in use stays dry until one is free (the INSERTS list shows how many are left). A saved project keeps the type, not the instance: on load the tracks get them in order T1 T2 T3 DR.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: JUNO CHORUS insert (the Juno-106 chorus)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The Juno-106's chorus as an insert type (INSERTS > S1 / S2, and the master's insert slots: JUNO): the MN3009 BBD model of fm-106, MODE I, II or I+II, JUNO its mix (127: the Juno's chorus on). A mono track comes out stereo. About 130 host instructions a sample an instance. 0 is off. Each instance is a line in the pool; a track that picks it when every instance is in use stays dry until one is free (the INSERTS list shows how many are left). A saved project keeps the type, not the instance: on load the tracks get them in order T1 T2 T3 DR.
items.notice: From fm-106 by PatttF (GPL-3.0), after Ultramaster KR-106 (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: fm-106 (PatttF/fm-106) @ be74757 by PatttF (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: EQ3 insert (three-band DJ EQ)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A three-band equaliser type, like Ableton's EQ Three, for any insert slot (a track's, a drum sound's, the master's) and the returns (EQ3): LO MID HI from KILL (the left end) to +6 dB, the crossovers FREQ LO (250 Hz) and FREQ HI (2.5 kHz) at 12 dB/oct (Linkwitz-Riley: the bands sum flat). All three at 0 dB is a bypass that costs nothing; moving in and out of it crossfades in 3 ms. About 75 host instructions a sample on a track.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: return feedback sends (B to A, C to A, C to B)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: The master's returns send to the returns on their left too (MASTER > A SENDS, B SENDS, C SENDS: each return to the other two), for feedback between the effects: a delay into a reverb and back. Each such send takes its return's output of the block before (a loop of 32 samples, 0.73 ms), DC-blocked, limited to -12 dBFS and soft-clipped, at a quarter of the gain of a send to the right, so no loop runs away. Without it a return sends only to its right (A to B and C, B to C). About 1.2 KB of RAM; nothing runs while every such send is 0.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: FLNG insert (flanger)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A flanger type for any insert slot (a track's, the master's, the USB input's) and the returns (FLNG): a short delay swept 0.25 .. 5 ms (~0.25 Hz); FLNG up to the middle mixes it in, past the middle adds feedback. 0 is off. Each instance is a line in the pool; a track that picks it when every instance is in use stays dry until one is free (the INSERTS list shows how many are left). A saved project keeps the type, not the instance: on load the tracks get them in order T1 T2 T3 DR.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT FLANG by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Felucca 1.5.6 (hugelton/Felucca) @ 9f6a885 by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: GATER insert (tempo-synced trance gate)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A rhythmic volume gate type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: GATER), locked to the tempo and the sequencer's steps (it restarts with PLAY, follows the swing): one of 16 built-in 16-step patterns (trance gates, 1/8 and 1/16 chops, offbeats, dotted, clave), a RATE of 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 or their triplets, DEPTH (the amount: how far a closed step closes, 0 off) and SHAPE (hard to smooth). Every track can run it at once.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: CHORD+ (black keys change the chord), STRUM, VLEAD
items.desc: With a chord mode on (SCL > CHORD), the black keys change the chord played: F# major <-> minor, G# adds the 7th, A# sus4, C# the 9th, D# inverts; hold several to combine, or press one while a chord is held. SCL 2 gains STRUM (1-60 ms a note, right low to high, left high to low; keys and chord steps) and VLEAD (each chord voiced nearest the last). Recorded as it sounds; MIDI out sends the chord unstrummed.
items.notice: From SLOOP 2.4's CHORD+ by isod89 (isod89/sloop-fm1 v2.4, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: SLOOP 2.4 (isod89/sloop-fm1) @ v2.4 8d3823f by isod89 (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: song sections
items.desc: 8 / 16: banks of 4 (SAVE + OCT), stored compressed in one 32 KiB log with a MEM gauge; the old slots move in at the first start. 4: the slots as before (needed by motion recording)

items.label: snapshots (whole-state slots)
items.desc: SAVE > SNAPSHOT: the working project, every section and the song in one slot, loaded back whole (the state before is kept in BEFORE LOAD); export / import in the web editor. The flash comes from the end of USR3 (slots + 4 sectors of 4 KiB): the user sample slot USR3 holds that much less (docs/SNAPSHOTS.md)

items.label: per-track patterns and scenes
items.desc: 16 patterns a track, stored in the section log; a section becomes a scene that names a pattern a track, so scenes share patterns and an unchanged track costs nothing. The old sections become scenes at the first start. LFO held: the PATTERN layer (launch at the end, the next bar or now; store, copy, clear); the web editor shows the slots in the mixer. About 6.1 KB of flash and 0.1 KB of RAM. Off: sections as before (a scene stored with patterns plays as the section it would be).

items.label: undo / redo history (many levels)
items.desc: Undo and redo of pattern edits (EDIT + OCT- / OCT+) over many levels; the history lives in the pool and RAM this build leaves free (at least 1 KiB). About 2.2 KB of flash; off: a single undo level.

items.label: performance macros (GLO > MACRO)
items.desc: COLOR, MOTION, SPACE, ENERGY: four knobs, each moving several sounds' parameters at once (filters and FM index, LFO depths, sends and width, drive and drum level), kept per project and section (the drum track's unused ENV / LFO DEST values: no format change); recorded by motion recording. At home: no change. About 1.4 KB of flash and 0.4 KB of RAM.
items.provenance_line: Flowstate (zakariachowdhury/flowstate-fm1) @ 3962560 by Zakaria Chowdhury (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: ENERGY bands thin / thicken the drums
items.desc: ENERGY also thins or thickens the drum pattern in five bands, walked on the beat: core lanes on the eighths, no ghosts, as written, harder hits, hat ratchets and a snare fill every second pass. About 0.6 KB of flash.
items.provenance_line: Flowstate (zakariachowdhury/flowstate-fm1) @ 3962560 by Zakaria Chowdhury (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: USB port
items.desc: What the USB port offers. USB MIDI (notes, clock, the editor and updates) is in every choice. MIDI only (default): nothing more (smallest). CDC console: a read-only serial console for diagnostics. USB audio + MIDI (EXPERIMENTAL): 4 stems in + stereo out (UAC1) next to USB MIDI; the stems are resampled to the computer's clock (cubic, after X0X 80b7d40), so a host passing the input live to an output does not drop out. It replaces the console and needs +12 KB pool (a resampler in the audio path is CPU-heavy). It streams on the FM-1 since 2026-10-12 (before, a USB audio build hung and went to the USB rescue); its audio quality is not checked yet.
items.notice: USB audio capture resampler ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), 80b7d40: part of the USB audio choice of this item.
items.provenance_line: Melodee (keremimo/melodee) by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: TRS MIDI IN
items.desc: MIDI input on the TRS jack (notes and clock from a keyboard or sequencer). About 0.6 KB of flash; off: the jack hears nothing, and SYNC TRS has no clock.

items.label: MIDI clock in + out
items.desc: MIDI clock both ways. In: follow an external MIDI clock and start / stop (GLO > SYSTEM SYNC: AUTO takes the TRS jack, else USB, else the internal tempo). Out: send MIDI clock on USB so a computer, drum machine or sequencer can follow the FM-1: 24 ticks a beat (also while stopped, so the other side has the tempo first), Start, Stop, and Song Position + Continue when the FM-1 itself continues an external song. Each tick leaves with the sound of its beat (latency-compensated, no jitter of its own), follows tempo changes and the nudge, and never swings. Switched on in the HOME menu (CLOCK OUT, off by default). While the FM-1 follows a USB clock nothing is sent back to USB; following the TRS jack, the clock is passed on to USB. The TRS jack is input only (no MIDI out on the FM-1's board). Off: the FM-1 always runs on its own tempo and sends no clock.

items.label: MIDI expression (bend, mod, sustain, RPN)
items.desc: Plays more than notes from MIDI: pitch bend, mod wheel, breath, foot, aftertouch, sustain pedal and pitch-bend range (RPN 0). About 0.5 KB of flash; off: only notes and the panic messages work.
items.provenance_line: Melodee (keremimo/melodee) @ 670193c by ChanceTheMaker, Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: MIDI note out of the sequencer (HOME menu MIDI OUT = SEQ)
items.desc: MIDI OUT = SEQ (SLOOP 2.4): what the sequencer, the arp and the rolls play also goes to MIDI out, each track on its channel, every note ended (STOP, a channel changed, back to KEYS). Switched in the HOME menu (MIDI OUT KEYS / SEQ). About 1.2 to 2.5 KB of flash, by build; off: the menu row goes and only the panel's keys go out.
items.provenance_line: SLOOP 2.4 (isod89/sloop-fm1) @ v2.4 8d3823f by isod89 (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: user interface: SLOOP's pages or the Optimist rows
items.desc: Which user interface the firmware is built with (docs/UI-OPTIMIST-DESIGN.md). SLOOP's (the default): pages opened by the buttons, the layers held. The Optimist UI, phase 1 of its design: every screen a list of rows, the cursor row's four values on the knobs; HOME is the mixer (SELECT the row, the knobs the four tracks), SOUND the track's pages as rows, PROJECT and SYSTEM; SAVE = YES, HOME = NO, one confirm for what destroys. Not built yet in it: STEP, SONG, the held layers (only PLAY and REC), the Felucca look. Its own code replaces SLOOP's UI code, so it is smaller (the measured sizes: docs/UI-OPTIMIST-DESIGN.md section 11).

items.label: parameter icons
items.desc: A small 12 x 12 icon beside each parameter label. About 5.4 KB of flash; off: no icons, and the labels get their full width back.

items.label: VIEW ALL overview (4 x 4 PAGEs)
items.desc: GLO > SYSTEM VIEW ALL: shows a whole page family at once, 4 rows x 4 knobs a PAGE, PAGE n/m. About 2.4 KB of flash; off: one page at a time.

items.label: ARP graph and ARP in VIEW ALL
items.desc: Shows the arpeggiator's graph and puts the ARP settings into VIEW ALL. About 0.6 KB of flash; off: the ARP graph and its VIEW ALL rows are not built.

items.label: say what a project uses and this build lacks
items.desc: 'MISSING: PHYS T2, KIT 909' in the top bar when a project, song section, user preset or kit uses an engine, kit, sample set or FX this build leaves out (once per item until power-off; never stalls the audio); SAVE > TOOLS > MISS lists them again. Off: they play their stand-ins silently (saves 1.5 KB of flash)

items.label: drum steps on the keys (SLOOP 2.4 'Drums with the keys')
items.desc: On the DRUMS grid page (SEQ tapped on the drum track) the 16 white keys are the 16 steps of the sound KNOB 1 picks: press to set a step (you hear the sound), again to clear it; the first four black keys pick the page of steps. You hear what you pick: the sound when KNOB 1 changes it (on the grid and in the SEQ layer), the step's sounds when KNOB 2 moves to it. SELECT switches grid and kit (it is the tempo there without this item). Extra: while playing, the page follows the playhead (black key 5 turns it on / off). SEQ + a white key picks the sound (the SEQ layer's keys are its sounds). With the automation store built (PLOCK, MICRO, FILLS, CHANCE, MOTION), a step key held past the HOLD time is a held step as in the SEQ layer of the synth tracks: KNOB 4 nudge, PRESETS lock value, ALGORITHM lock parameter, KNOB 2 chance, OCT+ fill, OCT- clear (all of it). No data change. About 1.4 KB of flash, 16 B of RAM; the audition runs in the audio interrupt (no fast RAM code). Off: the keys play the pads on the grid page, as before.
items.notice: After SLOOP 2.4 'Drums with the keys' by isod89 (GPL-3.0), idea first from PR #45 by Erick Buendia Barrientos (Erbubar23). Tested in the host UI tests only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: SLOOP 2.4 (isod89/sloop-fm1) @ v2.4 8d3823f by isod89 (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: favorites: mark sounds, browse only them
items.desc: SAVE > PRESETS (SLOOP's UI): KNOB 3 FAV marks the selected track's sound as a favorite (ON / OFF), KNOB 4 LIST shows ALL or only the favorites (the PRESETS knob and KNOB 1 then walk just those); a marked sound shows a star in the list. The Optimist UI: with the presets: SHIFT2 (OCT+ held) + PRESETS marks the sound playing, SHIFT2 + SELECT browses only the favorites, a star after a favorite's name in the toast and in PROJECT > USER (SHIFT2 + ITEM marks a slot). Up to 64 factory sounds (kept by engine and name: they stay marked over builds that leave engines out) and any of the 32 user presets (an erased preset loses its mark); the FM6 / CZ banks and the drum track have none. Kept with the settings (136 B at the end of the settings record: an older record reads whole with none; a build without this item keeps the rest and forgets them on its next save). About 1 KB of flash, 136 B of pool. Off: PRESETS KNOB 3 and 4 stay empty.
items.notice: After Felucca 1.6's favorites by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host UI and storage tests only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Felucca (hugelton/Felucca) by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: help line: what the knob changes, in words
items.desc: while a knob turns, the top bar (the live screens' header) names its value in plain words, e.g. 'Filter cutoff', 'Reverb send', until ~1 s after the last detent; only the lines of the features built (tools/param_help.json, also the web editor's tooltips). The Optimist UI (UI=1): the screen's last line, while a value turns and ~2 s after, and always on GLOBAL, SYSTEM and PROJECT (the cursor line, the hot action, '(asks)' where it asks first). About 5.5 KB of flash (UI=1: 7.7 KB, its own lines too; the texts packed), no RAM code

items.label: chord names on the STEP page
items.desc: SEQ > STEP shows a step of several notes by its chord in any inversion: C, Am, Bdim, Caug, Dsus2, Dsus4, E5, G7, Fmaj7, F#m7, Bm7b5. Other note sets stay a note and the count ('C4 +2'). About 0.3 KB of flash; off: the step's first note and the count.
items.provenance_line: SLOOP 8-track PR (isod89/sloop-fm1 #45) @ 8d9623f by Erick Buendia Barrientos (Erbubar23) (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: knob acceleration by turn speed
items.desc: 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 8 steps a detent when turned fast; never on lists (engines, kits, presets)
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): knob acceleration. Tested in the emulator only.
items.provenance_line: X0X (charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) @ 61654ba by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: screen data speed (SPI clock)
items.desc: How fast data is sent to the display: 60 MHz / (n + 1). Faster redraws finish sooner (less tearing); the ST7789V takes ~62 MHz, so 60 MHz is the limit. No flash cost; the faster settings are untested here on hardware.
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): the faster LCD clock ran on X0X's FM-1; untested on hardware here.
items.provenance_line: X0X (charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) @ d179e03 by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: screen: send only the changed rectangle
items.desc: Redraws only the part of the graph strip that changed instead of the whole strip: less data per frame and less tearing (with the 30 MHz screen clock). Costs about 1.5 KB of flash and 0.6 KB of RAM.
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): dirty-rectangle screen updates. Not yet tried on hardware here.
items.provenance_line: X0X (charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) @ 201b95c by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: web editor and firmware updates (M-UPGRADE)
items.desc: The USB SysEx side of the device: the web editor (editing, presets, samples, backup / restore, snapshots), firmware updates from the M-UPGRADE tool and the rescue updater. About 18 KB of flash and 6 KB of RAM; leave it on unless you update through the UBOOT rescue path.
items.off_warning: without it there is no web editor (so no backup / restore from it) and no M-UPGRADE updates: updating needs the UBOOT rescue path

items.label: backup / restore from the web editor
items.desc: everything in flash to one .optimist-backup file and back (editor cmds 43..48); a restore onto another build reports what it skips and what plays a stand-in
items.off_warning: no backup: export projects and kits one by one before an update

items.label: web editor: every effect slot and its parameters (cmd 94)
items.desc: the web editor's FX slots by owner (track inserts, the drum bus and lane inserts, master inserts, returns, the USB input): type list, each type's own parameters (cmd 94 FXP, INFO tag 0x57). Off: the editor's Inserts / Returns pop-ups and the FX slot pages are not offered (the older FX command, 86, keeps its three send effects). About 5.3 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: drum lanes' mix, LFOs and mutes (cmd 95)
items.desc: the web editor's drum lane pan / mute / solo / sequencer mute, the lane's own LFO and the tracks' sequencer mutes (cmd 95 DLAN, INFO tag 0x58). Off: the lane pop-up keeps its older knobs; no lane LFO, mute or solo from the editor. About 1.6 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: GLOBAL and SYSTEM settings (cmd 96)
items.desc: the web editor's Device settings: GLOBAL and SYSTEM as the Optimist UI's lines, with their help (cmd 96 SCRN, INFO tag 0x59). Needs the Optimist UI (UI=1: with SLOOP's UI nothing is built). Off: the editor's Device-lines settings are hidden. About 1.3 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: the song chain (cmd 97)
items.desc: the web editor's song chain: PART 1..64 (scene, bars), INSERT / DELETE, LOOP / SONG, SAVE (cmd 97 SONGC, INFO tag 0x5A). Off: the editor's song chain editor is hidden. About 0.7 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: pattern tools and EUCLID (cmd 98)
items.desc: the web editor's pattern tools REVERSE, RANDOM, COOK, LENGTH x2 / 1/2 and EUCLID, run by the device's own function (cmd 98 TOOLS, INFO tag 0x5B). Needs the Optimist UI and SEQTOOLS. Off: the editor's tools buttons are hidden. About 0.8 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: the Optimist UI's screens as rows of cards (cmd 99)
items.desc: the web editor's Device screens tab: SOUND, MIX, MASTER, PROJECT, STEPS, SONG and TEMPO pages as the device shows them, any track, lane or FM6 operator (cmd 99 SCRS, INFO tag 0x5C). Needs the Optimist UI (UI=1). Off: no Device screens tab; the editor keeps its own Sound / Mixer / Sequence tabs. About 2.8 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: favorites (cmd 100)
items.desc: the web editor's stars in Load preset and its favorites-only list (cmd 100 FAVS, INFO tag 0x5D). Needs the favorites (FAVORITES). Off: no stars in the editor. About 1.0 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: the oscilloscope (cmd 101)
items.desc: the web editor's Device screens > SCOPE: the device's own trace of the master or a track (cmd 101 SCOPE, INFO tag 0x5E). Needs the Optimist UI (UI=1). Off: no scope in the editor. About 0.6 KB of flash (measured with the Optimist UI). The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: undo and redo (cmd 102)
items.desc: the web editor's UNDO and REDO of the patterns through the device's own undo history (cmd 102 UNDO, INFO tag 0x5F); with it built the editor's own step, lock, nudge, fill and chance writes are undo levels, as a panel step key's are (writes to one track within 800 ms are one level). Off: no undo in the editor. The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: play notes from the editor (cmd 103)
items.desc: the web editor's keyboard: a note on / off for a track through the device's own note input (the arp, the chord layout, the voice budget, REC and MIDI OUT KEYS apply), a ring to the audio interrupt of its own, at most 8 notes held, and an automatic note off after 3 s without a request from the host, on a USB reset, or after a given length (cmd 103 NOTE, INFO tag 0x60). Off: the editor cannot play notes. The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: track and lane solo and mute (cmd 104)
items.desc: the web editor's track and drum-lane SOLO and MUTE through the device's own masks (cmd 104 SOLO, INFO tag 0x61): the same state GLO + key 1..8 and the lane rows set. Off: the strip's SOLO stays a label. The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: web editor: a step in a drum lane, its lockable values (cmd 105)
items.desc: the web editor's held step in a track and drum-lane context: level, ratchet, chance, condition, nudge, fill, and the device's own list of lockable values (the Optimist UI's lock pages, a drum lane's TUNE .. LEVEL) with the locks and hold events on the step (cmd 105 STEPLANE, INFO tag 0x62). Needs the automation store. Off: the editor lists raw parameter ids and has no lane context. The INFO tag is sent only when it is built, and the editor hides what it does not find.

items.label: sound tables and FM6 buffers in the pool, not main RAM
items.desc: Moves what the sound loops read from main RAM to the pool: the sine, soft-clip and GRAIN window tables (about 2.5 KB, copied there from flash at start-up) and FM6's sine table, operator buses and voices (about 5.9 KB), so builder items get that much more main RAM. Unverified on hardware: both are the same SRAM as far as is known and the emulator cannot tell a speed difference, so on the FM-1 it may be slower; compare the console's TABBENCH figures and the CPU meter with it off and on. The sound is the same.

items.label: predictive CPU guard (ease back before shedding)
items.desc: Avoids audio dropouts under heavy load by easing quality back step by step before cutting notes. Under overload (the measured load or the one predicted from the voices sounding, over 85 % for 8 halves, or a late half): first ACID without oversampling and ANALOG 2's swarm at 2 copies, then UNISON at 2 voices, then voices shed, never the bass or the lead (MONO / LEGATO / UNISON parts) nor the drums; back after 2 s under 80 % counting what each step saved. The CPU meter shows %G1..%G3. Weights: tools/builder/cpu_costs.py from tests/cpu_baseline.txt (docs/CPU-GUARD.md)
items.provenance_line: Flowstate (zakariachowdhury/flowstate-fm1) @ e62e186 by Zakaria Chowdhury (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: hand-written assembly speed-ups (FM6, ANALOG 2)
items.desc: The hottest loops of FM6 and ANALOG 2 written in the processor's assembly: the same sound, about 8 to 19 % less audio CPU (emulator), for about 0.6 KB of flash and 0.7 KB of fast RAM code. Keep on; off only to compare with the plain C.

items.label: second CPU core renders parts 2-3 (EXPERIMENTAL)
items.desc: Experimental: the FM-1's second CPU core renders synth parts 2 and 3 while the first renders the rest, cutting the first core's load by 40 to 44 % in the emulator, with the same sound. It costs about 1.8 KB of flash, 1.9 KB of RAM and 6 KB of pool. On some FM-1s the second core misreads RAM at the boot loader's supply: it then runs nothing it misread, is held for the session and the FM-1 goes on with one core (the message CPU1 OFF MISREAD); a boot after one that crashed in its first 30 s stays on one core.
items.notice: Its guard against misread RAM is ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): the second core runs only the next job, with a matching check word, and is held at the first one it refuses.
items.tested: emulator-tested; one user's FM-1 runs it
items.provenance_line: X0X (charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) @ 47f8e4c by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: raise the core rails to the FM-1's stock values at start-up (for the second core)
items.desc: At start-up, before the second core, the audio and Bluetooth, the FM-1's rails are set as its own M-VAVE firmware sets them: the 1.4 V rail moved from its LDO to the DC-DC, then raised to 1.60 V (VDC14 7), then the core rail to 1.38 V (SYSVDD 15), a step at a time, never lowered (the boot loader leaves 1.40 V and 1.26 V). Read back after: if a value is wrong, the second core stays off (2ND CORE OFF SUPPLY) and the FM-1 runs on one core. SYSTEM > INTERNALS shows the rails (SUPPLY). Second-core builds only; it replaces the earlier DUAL_BOOST (1.50 V / 1.38 V on the LDO). On the second core's test unit both cores crashed within seconds at the boot loader's rails and ran 3 x 3 minutes with 1.50 V / 1.38 V; the stock sequence itself is still being measured.
items.notice: EXPERIMENTAL, at your own risk: the FM-1's own firmware raises its rails this way, every custom firmware leaves them at the boot loader's lower levels. 1.38 V core and 1.60 V on the 1.4 V rail are above the AC79 datasheet's table (the chip's absolute limits are not public); chips vary from unit to unit; the effect on heat and battery life has not been measured.
items.tested: the sequence emulator- and host-tested; 1.50 V / 1.38 V measured on one FM-1 (2026-10-16)
items.provenance_line: Melodee (keremimo/melodee) @ 7a51700 by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: Bluetooth LE MIDI, our own stack (EXPERIMENTAL)
items.desc: Experimental: BLE MIDI as the stock firmware offers it (named FM-1 XXXX, the BLE-MIDI service), from a stack written for Optimist (docs/BLE-STACK.md): BLE in plays the synth, the FM-1's own notes go out with real timestamps. Tested on an FM-1 with macOS Audio MIDI Setup (not yet with iOS or Windows). The radio's start-up tables, captured from the stock V15 firmware, are included: no V15 file is needed (FM1_STOCK_FWSC makes a fresh capture instead, with the same result). Bluetooth starts OFF: switch it on in HOME > MENU > BLUETOOTH. MIDI IN must be NOTES for notes to play (HOME menu SYSTEM). About 30 KB of flash and 6 KB of RAM (the menu shows the measured figures; BLE_DIAG below adds more); where the build then overflows, ticking it removes the smallest single item that frees enough (sample sets first, then other items), or the one you pick instead.
items.tested: tested on an FM-1 with macOS Audio MIDI Setup, not yet with iOS or Windows

items.label: BLE diagnostics: the console's blell, counters and rings
items.desc: Experimental, for finding BLE faults: the console's blell command (needs a CDC / console build, USB_MODE 1) and the counters and rings behind it (link-layer events, the radio's receive and transmit state, the protocol packets, BLE-MIDI in). About 6 KB of flash and 2.3 KB of RAM, and 6 KB of flash more with the console (USB_MODE 1) for blell itself. Leave it off for normal use: BLE works the same without it; bletrim and blevm stay, and so does the boot breadcrumb.

items.label: BLE bonding: pairing (Just Works) and an encrypted link
items.desc: Experimental: LE legacy pairing with Just Works (no passkey, as the FM-1 has no screen keypad for it) and bonding, so a Mac or phone that pairs once gets an encrypted link and finds the FM-1 bonded after a power-off. The FM-1 hands out its identity and takes the other side's (its IRK and identity address, kept until power-off for now), which reconnecting to devices with private addresses needs later. Pairing happens only when the other side asks for it. Not yet tested on an FM-1. About 6.7 KB of flash and 0.7 KB of RAM.

items.label: BLE devices: connect to BLE-MIDI devices, reconnect the last one
items.desc: Experimental: HOME > MENU > BLUETOOTH > DEVICES lists the BLE-MIDI devices nearby (keyboards, controllers, a Mac or an iPhone app that advertises BLE MIDI, another FM-1) with their names and relative signal bars, scanning only while the list is open (the FM-1 stops advertising meanwhile). Picking one connects to it as a central (pairing with Just Works when it asks, as Apple's devices do), MIDI both ways; it becomes the last device, which the FM-1 reconnects to by itself while Bluetooth is on. Brings the bonding of BLE_BOND with it. Without this item DEVICES shows NONE and the last device only. Not yet tested on an FM-1.
